parts.latex: Find an expression for the $n$th term of the arithmetic sequence $100, 92, 84, \dots$?

solutions.latex:
The sequence is arithmetic with first term and common difference
$$a=100,\quad d=-8$$
Using the formula for the $n$th term:

parts.latex: Find the limiting sum of the geometric series $1-\dfrac{1}{3}+\dfrac{1}{9}-\dfrac{1}{27}+\dots$.

solutions.latex:
The series is geometric with
$$a=1,\quad r=-\dfrac{1}{3}$$
Since $|r|<1$, the limiting sum exists:
$$\begin{aligned} S_\infty &= \dfrac{a}{1-r} \\ &= \dfrac{1}{1-\left(-\frac{1}{3}\right)} \\ &= \dfrac{3}{4} \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ S_\infty = \dfrac{3}{4}$$

What is the probability that both coins land showing heads?

Both coins have the same bias, so
$$P(T)\times P(T)=0.49$$
$$P(T)=\sqrt{0.49}=0.7$$
Hence
$$P(H)=1-0.7=0.3$$
$$\begin{aligned} P(HH) &= 0.3\times 0.3 \\ &= 0.09 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ P(HH)=0.09$$

The probabilities sum to 1:
$$0.1+0.3+n+0.2=1$$
so $n=0.4$.

The expected value is
$$\begin{aligned} E(X) &= 4(0.1)+5(0.3)+6(0.4)+7(0.2) \\ &= 5.7 \end{aligned}$$
The variance is
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Var}(X) &= 4^2(0.1)+5^2(0.3)+6^2(0.4)+7^2(0.2)-5.7^2 \\ &= 33.3-32.49 \\ &= 0.81 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ E(X)=5.7,\quad \text{Var}(X)=0.81$$

On what day of training will she run further than 25 km for the first time?

$$a=10,\quad r=1.1,\quad T_n=ar^{n-1}$$
Test the 10th and 11th days:

so the 11th day.

2464.stem: A standard six-sided die is marked with the numbers $1, 2, \dots, 6$. A game is played by rolling the die until a 6 appears on the uppermost face. At this point the game ends.

parts.latex:
Using a tree diagram, or otherwise, explain why the probability of the game ending before the fourth roll is:

$$\dfrac{1}{6}+\dfrac{5}{6}\times\dfrac{1}{6}+\left(\dfrac{5}{6}\right)^2\times\dfrac{1}{6}$$
What is the smallest value of $n$ for which the probability of the game ending before the $n$th roll is more than $90\%$?

solutions.latex:
On each roll, $P(6)=\dfrac{1}{6}$ and $P(\text{not } 6)=\dfrac{5}{6}$.

In the tree diagram, at each roll the game ends with probability $\dfrac{1}{6}$ or continues with probability $\dfrac{5}{6}$.

The game ends before the 4th roll if it ends on the 1st, 2nd or 3rd roll:
$$\begin{aligned} P(\text{ends before 4th roll}) &= \dfrac{1}{6}+\dfrac{5}{6}\times\dfrac{1}{6}+\dfrac{5}{6}\times\dfrac{5}{6}\times\dfrac{1}{6} \\ &= \dfrac{1}{6}+\dfrac{5}{6}\times\dfrac{1}{6}+\left(\dfrac{5}{6}\right)^2\times\dfrac{1}{6} \end{aligned}$$
as required.
criteria: Draws tree diagram or sets up correct reasoning, or equivalent merit

meta.format_note: Alternate solution (add the probabilities of winning on rolls 1, 2, 3) folded into the working. A tree diagram is not drawn.

solutions.latex:
The game ends before the $n$th roll if it ends on one of rolls $1$ to $n-1$:
$$P(\text{ends before } n\text{th roll})=\left(\dfrac{5}{6}\right)^0\dfrac{1}{6}+\left(\dfrac{5}{6}\right)^1\dfrac{1}{6}+\dots+\left(\dfrac{5}{6}\right)^{n-2}\dfrac{1}{6}$$
This is a geometric series with $a=\dfrac{1}{6}$, $r=\dfrac{5}{6}$ and $n-1$ terms:
$$\begin{aligned} S_{n-1} &= \dfrac{\frac{1}{6}\left(1-\left(\frac{5}{6}\right)^{n-1}\right)}{1-\frac{5}{6}} \\ &= 1-\left(\dfrac{5}{6}\right)^{n-1} \end{aligned}$$
We need this to exceed $0.9$. Solve the equality first:
$$\begin{aligned} 0.9 &= 1-\left(\dfrac{5}{6}\right)^{n-1} \\ \left(\dfrac{5}{6}\right)^{n-1} &= 0.1 \\ (n-1)\log\dfrac{5}{6} &= \log 0.1 \\ n-1 &= \dfrac{\log 0.1}{\log\frac{5}{6}} = 12.629\dots \\ n &= 13.629\dots \end{aligned}$$
$n$ must be a whole number, so we round up.
$$\therefore\ \text{the smallest value of } n \text{ is } 14$$
criteria: Correct simplified equation to solve, or equivalent merit

2467.stem:
In a reducing balance loan, an amount $\$P$ is borrowed for a period of $n$ months at an interest rate of $0.4\%$ per month, compounded monthly. At the end of each month a repayment of $\$M$ is made. After the $n$th repayment has been made the amount owing, $\$A_n$ is given by:

$$A_n = P(1.004)^n - M\left(1+(1.004)^1+(1.004)^2+\dots+(1.004)^{n-1}\right)$$

(Do NOT prove this.)

parts.latex:
Celeste borrows \$500 000 in a reducing balance loan as described. The loan is to be repaid in 240 monthly repayments.

Show that $M = \$3244.79$, when rounded to the nearest cent.

After 150 repayments of \$3244.79 have been made, the interest rate changes to $0.5\%$ per month.

At this stage the amount owing to the nearest dollar is \$244 837. (Do NOT prove this.)

Celeste increases her monthly repayments to \$3500.

For how many months will Celeste need to make full monthly repayments of \$3500?

criteria: Sums the geometric series, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
The new rate is $0.5\%$ per month, so the monthly factor is $1.005$. Starting from $\$244\,837$:
$$\begin{aligned} A_1 &= 244\,837\times 1.005-3500 \\ A_2 &= 244\,837\times 1.005^2-3500\times 1.005-3500 \end{aligned}$$
Continuing, and summing the geometric series:
$$\begin{aligned} A_n &= 244\,837\times 1.005^n-3500\left(1+1.005+\dots+1.005^{n-1}\right) \\ &= 244\,837\times 1.005^n-\dfrac{3500(1.005^n-1)}{0.005} \end{aligned}$$
Set $A_n=0$:
$$\begin{aligned} 3500(1.005^n-1) &= 244\,837\times 1.005^n\times 0.005 \\ 3500\times 1.005^n-3500 &= 1224.185\times 1.005^n \\ 2275.815\times 1.005^n &= 3500 \\ 1.005^n &= \dfrac{3500}{2275.815} \\ n &= \dfrac{\log\left(\frac{3500}{2275.815}\right)}{\log 1.005} = 86.299\dots \end{aligned}$$
The loan is not cleared after 86 repayments, so the last payment is smaller.
$$\therefore\ \text{86 full payments of } \$3500 \text{ are made}$$
criteria: Sets up correct equation to solve for $n$, or equivalent merit

The graph of the function $f(x)=8x^2$ is translated $b$ units to the left, then dilated horizontally by a scale factor of $a$ with $a>0$ and then translated $c$ units up. The equation of the transformed function is $g(x)=2x^2+4x+21$.

Find possible values of $a$, $b$ and $c$.

solutions.latex:
Translating $b$ units left gives $8(x+b)^2$.

Dilating horizontally by factor $a$ replaces $x$ with $\dfrac{x}{a}$, giving $8\left(\dfrac{x}{a}+b\right)^2$.

Translating $c$ units up gives $8\left(\dfrac{x}{a}+b\right)^2+c$.

Equate to $g(x)$ and expand:

$$8\left(\dfrac{x}{a}+b\right)^2+c\equiv 2x^2+4x+21$$

$$\dfrac{8}{a^2}x^2+\dfrac{16b}{a}x+(8b^2+c)\equiv 2x^2+4x+21$$

Equating coefficients of $x^2$:

$$\dfrac{8}{a^2}=2$$

so $a=2$, since $a>0$.

Equating coefficients of $x$:

$$\dfrac{16b}{a}=4$$

so $b=\dfrac{1}{2}$.

Equating constants: $8b^2+c=21$, so $c=19$.

$$\therefore\ a=2,\ b=\dfrac{1}{2},\ c=19$$

The alternative working with a translation $b$ to the right gives $a=2$, $b=-\dfrac{1}{2}$, $c=19$.

parts.latex: Consider the curve $y=2x^3-6x^2$.
Find the stationary points and determine their nature.
Find any points of inflection. Make sure you justify your answer(s).
Sketch the curve showing the stationary points and the point of inflection.

solutions.latex:
Stationary points occur where $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=0$.

$$\dfrac{dy}{dx}=6x^2-12x=6x(x-2)=0$$

So $x=0$ or $x=2$.

When $x=0$, $y=0$. When $x=2$, $y=2(8)-6(4)=-8$.

The stationary points are $(0,0)$ and $(2,-8)$.

Test the nature using the second derivative:

$$\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}=12x-12$$

$$\begin{aligned} \text{At } x=0:\ \dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} &= -12<0 &&\text{maximum turning point}\\ \text{At } x=2:\ \dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} &= 12>0 &&\text{minimum turning point} \end{aligned}$$

A table of values of $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ either side of each point is an equivalent justification.

$$\therefore\ (0,0)\text{ is a maximum and }(2,-8)\text{ is a minimum}$$
criteria: Finds both stationary points and the second derivative, or equivalent merit
Finds the stationary points, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
A point of inflection needs $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}=0$ and a change in concavity.

$$12x-12=0$$

So $x=1$, and $y=2-6=-4$.

Test the concavity either side of $x=1$:

$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} &< 0 &&\text{for } x<1 &&\text{concave down}\\ \dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} &> 0 &&\text{for } x>1 &&\text{concave up} \end{aligned}$$

The concavity changes at $x=1$.

$$\therefore\ (1,-4)\text{ is a point of inflection}$$

parts.latex:
A pipe costs \$4000/km when laid on land and \$5000/km when laid under the ocean.

In the diagram below a pipeline needs to be laid from $A$ along a coast to $B$ on an island. The pipe is to be laid in straight lines from $A$ on land along the coast until $C$ and then under the ocean to $B$.

Let $x=CD$.

\exfigure{1597_q5b_1}
Write an expression for the total price (\$$P$) of laying the cable from $A$ to $B$ via $C$ in terms of $x$.
Find the length for $x$ that will minimise the total price (\$$P$) of laying the whole pipe from $A$ to $B$ via $C$.

solutions.latex:
The land section is $AC=10-x$ km at \$4000/km, and the ocean section $CB$ is the hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle with sides $6$ and $x$, so $CB=\sqrt{36+x^2}$ km at \$5000/km (Pythagoras' theorem).

$$P=4000(10-x)+5000\sqrt{36+x^2}$$

meta.format_note: Lengths 10 and 6 read from the source expression (figure not visible here).

solutions.latex:
$P$ is minimised where $\dfrac{dP}{dx}=0$.

$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{dP}{dx} &= -4000+5000\times\dfrac{1}{2}(36+x^2)^{-\frac{1}{2}}\times 2x \\ &= \dfrac{5000x}{\sqrt{36+x^2}}-4000 \end{aligned}$$

Set this to zero:

$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{5x}{\sqrt{36+x^2}} &= 4 \\ 25x^2 &= 16(36+x^2) \\ 9x^2 &= 576 \\ x^2 &= 64 \end{aligned}$$

So $x=\pm 8$. Since $0\le x\le 10$, $x=8$ only.

First derivative test:

$$\begin{aligned} \text{At } x=7:\ \dfrac{dP}{dx} &\approx -204<0 &&\text{decreasing}\\ \text{At } x=9:\ \dfrac{dP}{dx} &\approx 160>0 &&\text{increasing} \end{aligned}$$

So a relative minimum occurs at $x=8$.

Check against the end points:

$$\begin{aligned} P(0) &= \$70\,000 \\ P(10) &\approx \$58\,310 \\ P(8) &= \$58\,000 \end{aligned}$$

So $x=8$ gives the absolute minimum on $[0,10]$.

Alternatively, by the second derivative test:

$$\dfrac{d^2P}{dx^2}=\dfrac{180\,000}{(36+x^2)^{\frac{3}{2}}}$$

which equals $180>0$ at $x=8$.

$$\therefore\ CD=8 \text{ km}$$

2487.stem:
A radioactive substance decays at a rate proportional to the mass present.

The rate of change is given by $\dfrac{dM}{dt} = -kM$, where $k$ is a positive constant and $M$ grams is the mass present at any time, $t$ years.

parts.latex: Show that $M = 75e^{-kt}$ is a solution to this equation.
If $68$g remains after a period of $2$ years, find $k$ correct to two significant figures.

Find the mass of the substance that remains after $6$ years.

Give your answer to one decimal place.
At what rate is the substance decaying after $6$ years ?

solutions.latex:
Differentiate $M = 75e^{-kt}$ with respect to $t$.
$$\dfrac{dM}{dt} = -k\cdot 75e^{-kt}$$
But $75e^{-kt} = M$, so
$$\dfrac{dM}{dt} = -kM$$
Hence $M = 75e^{-kt}$ is a solution.

Substitute $M=68$ and $t=2$ into $M = 75e^{-kt}$.
$$\begin{aligned} 68 &= 75e^{-2k} \\ \dfrac{68}{75} &= e^{-2k} \\ -2k &= \ln\left(\dfrac{68}{75}\right) \\ k &= -\dfrac{1}{2}\ln\left(\dfrac{68}{75}\right) \\ &\approx 0.049 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ k \approx 0.049$$

Substitute $t=6$ and $k \approx 0.049$ into $M = 75e^{-kt}$.
$$\begin{aligned} M &= 75e^{-6k} \\ &\approx 55.9 \text{ g} \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ M \approx 55.9 \text{ g}$$

meta.format_note: 55.9 g follows from using the rounded $k=0.049$ from part (b).

solutions.latex:
The rate of decay is given by $\dfrac{dM}{dt} = -kM$, with $k \approx 0.049$ and $M \approx 55.9$.
$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{dM}{dt} &= -kM \\ &\approx -2.7 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{the substance is decaying at approximately } 2.7 \text{ g/year}$$

2489.stem: The velocity, $\dot{x}$, of a particle moving in a straight line is given by $\dot{x} = \cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}t\right)$, where $x$ is in metres and $t$ is in seconds. The particle is initially at the origin.

parts.latex: Find the initial velocity.
Find an expression for the displacement of the particle, $x$, in terms of $t$.
Find when the particle first comes to rest.
Find the distance travelled by the particle in the first $7$ seconds.

solutions.latex:
Substitute $t=0$ into the velocity.
$$\begin{aligned} \dot{x} &= \cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\cdot 0\right) \\ &= \cos 0 \\ &= 1 \text{ m/s} \end{aligned}$$

Displacement is the integral of velocity.
$$x = \dfrac{6}{\pi}\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}t\right) + C$$
When $t = 0$, $x = 0$, so $C = 0$.
$$\therefore\ x = \dfrac{6}{\pi}\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}t\right)$$

The particle is at rest when $\dot{x} = 0$.
$$\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}t\right) = 0$$
The first positive solution of $\cos\theta=0$ is $\theta=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$.
$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{\pi}{6}t &= \dfrac{\pi}{2} \\ t &= 3 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ t = 3 \text{ seconds}$$

The particle is at rest at $t=3$ and then reverses, so find the distance in two stages.
$$\begin{aligned} x(3) &= \dfrac{6}{\pi}\sin\dfrac{\pi}{2} \\ &= \dfrac{6}{\pi} \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} x(7) &= \dfrac{6}{\pi}\sin\dfrac{7\pi}{6} \\ &= \dfrac{6}{\pi}\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right) \\ &= -\dfrac{3}{\pi} \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Distance travelled} &= \dfrac{6}{\pi} + \left(\dfrac{6}{\pi} + \dfrac{3}{\pi}\right) \\ &= \dfrac{15}{\pi} \text{ m} \end{aligned}$$

parts.latex: Find the $x$ coordinate(s) of any stationary point(s) on the graph of $y = e^{2x}(1 - x)$. You do not need to determine the nature.

solutions.latex:
Using the product rule, $\dfrac{d}{dx}(uv)=u'v+uv'$, with
$$\begin{aligned} u&=e^{2x} & v&=1-x\\ u'&=2e^{2x} & v'&=-1\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} y' &= -e^{2x} + 2e^{2x}(1-x) \\ &= -e^{2x} + 2e^{2x} - 2xe^{2x} \\ &= e^{2x}(1-2x) \end{aligned}$$
Stationary points occur when $y'=0$. Since $e^{2x} \neq 0$, we need $1-2x=0$.
$$\therefore\ x = \dfrac{1}{2}$$

2493.stem:
An iron has accidently been left on. Fortunately, it switches itself off automatically after a period of inactivity.

The temperature of the iron can be modelled by the equation $T = 20 + 155(1.2)^{-0.4t}$, where $T$ is the temperature of the iron's surface, in degrees Celsius, $t$ minutes after the iron switches itself off.

parts.latex:
What is the temperature of the iron $8$ minutes after it has switched off ?

Give your answer to the nearest degree.

At what rate is the temperature of the iron's surface changing after $8$ minutes ?

(Give your answer to one decimal place.)
How long, to the nearest minute, will it take for the iron to cool to $36^\circ\text{C}$ ?
What will be the eventual temperature of the iron ?

solutions.latex:
Substitute $t=8$.
$$\begin{aligned} T &= 20 + 155(1.2)^{-0.4(8)} \\ &\approx 106^\circ\text{C} \end{aligned}$$

Using $\dfrac{d}{dt}a^{kt} = k a^{kt}\ln a$:
$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{dT}{dt} &= -0.4\left(155(1.2)^{-0.4t}\right)\ln(1.2) \\ &= -62(1.2)^{-0.4t}\ln(1.2) \end{aligned}$$
When $t = 8$:
$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{dT}{dt} &= -62(1.2)^{-3.2}\ln(1.2) \\ &\approx -6.3^\circ\text{C/min} \end{aligned}$$

Set $T=36$ and solve for $t$, taking logarithms of both sides.
$$\begin{aligned}36 &= 20 + 155(1.2)^{-0.4t}\\ 16 &= 155(1.2)^{-0.4t}\\ \dfrac{16}{155} &= 1.2^{-0.4t}\\ \ln\left(\dfrac{16}{155}\right) &= -0.4t\ln(1.2)\\ t &= \dfrac{-\ln\left(\frac{16}{155}\right)}{0.4\ln 1.2} \\ &\approx 31\text{ minutes}\end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ t \approx 31 \text{ minutes}$$
criteria: Obtains $\dfrac{16}{155} = 1.2^{-0.4t}$ or an expression for $t$, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
Using the product rule, $\dfrac{d}{dx}(uv)=u'v+uv'$, with
$$\begin{aligned} u&=x & v&=\cos 2x\\ u'&=1 & v'&=-2\sin 2x\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned}\dfrac{d}{dx}(x\cos 2x) &= x(-2\sin 2x) + \cos 2x(1)\\ &= -2x\sin 2x + \cos 2x\\ &= \cos 2x - 2x\sin 2x\end{aligned}$$

Integrate the result of part (a) over the interval, since integration reverses differentiation.
$$\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{6}}(\cos 2x - 2x\sin 2x)\,dx = \Big[x\cos 2x\Big]_0^{\frac{\pi}{6}}$$
Rearranging,
$$\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{6}} 2x\sin 2x\,dx = \int_0^{\frac{\pi}{6}}\cos 2x\,dx - \Big[x\cos 2x\Big]_0^{\frac{\pi}{6}}$$
$$\begin{aligned}&= \left[\dfrac{1}{2}\sin 2x\right]_0^{\frac{\pi}{6}} - \Big[x\cos 2x\Big]_0^{\frac{\pi}{6}}\\ &= \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\sin\dfrac{\pi}{3} - \dfrac{1}{2}\sin 0\right) - \left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\cos\dfrac{\pi}{3} - 0\right)\\ &= \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{4} - \dfrac{\pi}{12}\\ &= \dfrac{3\sqrt{3} - \pi}{12}\end{aligned}$$

parts.latex:

parts.latex: Find the second derivative of $y=x\left(x+1\right)^3$, leaving your answer in fully factorised form.

$$\begin{aligned} u&=x & v&=(x+1)^3\\ u'&=1 & v'&=3(x+1)^2\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} y'&=(x+1)^3\times1+3(x+1)^2\times x \\ &=(x+1)^2\left[(x+1)+3x\right] \\ &=(x+1)^2(4x+1) \end{aligned}$$
Applying the product rule again, with
$$\begin{aligned} u&=(x+1)^2 & v&=4x+1\\ u'&=2(x+1) & v'&=4\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} y''&=(4x+1)\times2(x+1)+(x+1)^2\times4 \\ &=2(x+1)\left[4x+1+2(x+1)\right] \\ &=2(x+1)(6x+3) \\ &=6(x+1)(2x+1) \end{aligned}$$

A rainwater tank manufacturer wants to make a new storage tank that has a standard height, to reduce the obstruction of views. parts.latex: Show that for the given capacity of the tank, $y=\dfrac{3}{x}$
Hence, calculate the exact dimensions of the tank that uses the least amount of area of sheet metal as possible. Show all reasoning.

solutions.latex:
Convert the capacity: $6000\text{ L}=6\text{ m}^3$.

The volume of the prism is length $\times$ width $\times$ height:
$$\begin{aligned} x\times y\times2&=6 \\ 2xy&=6 \\ y&=\dfrac{6}{2x} \\ &=\dfrac{3}{x} \end{aligned}$$

The surface area is the top and bottom plus four sides:
$$A=2(xy+2x+2y)=2xy+4x+4y$$
Substituting $y=\dfrac{3}{x}$:
$$A=4x+\dfrac{12}{x}+6$$
Differentiating:
$$\dfrac{dA}{dx}=4-\dfrac{12}{x^2}$$
For a minimum, $\dfrac{dA}{dx}=0$:
$$\begin{aligned} 4x^2&=12 \\ x^2&=3 \end{aligned}$$
So $x=\sqrt{3}$, since $x>0$.

Test the nature using the second derivative:
$$\dfrac{d^2A}{dx^2}=\dfrac{24}{x^3}>0 \text{ for all } x>0$$
So the curve is concave up and the area is a minimum at $x=\sqrt{3}$.

Then $y=\dfrac{3}{\sqrt{3}}=\sqrt{3}$.

$$\therefore\ \text{dimensions } \sqrt{3}\text{ m}\times\sqrt{3}\text{ m}\times2\text{ m}$$

A quantity $Q$ of the radioactive isotope Carbon-14 decays according the equation of natural decay $Q=Q_0e^{-kt}$ where $Q_0$ is the initial mass of Carbon-14, $k$ is a constant and $t$ is the time in years.

The half-life of a radioactive substance is the time it takes to reduce to half its original mass. Carbon-14 has a half-life of 5730 years.

parts.latex: Find the exact value of $k$.

A fossilised leaf contains $9\%$ of its original amount of Carbon-14.

How old is the fossilised leaf? Give your answer correct to the nearest year.

solutions.latex:
After one half-life, $Q=\dfrac{Q_0}{2}$ when $t=5730$.
$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{Q_0}{2} &= Q_0e^{-5730k} \\ 0.5 &= e^{-5730k} \\ \ln0.5 &= -5730k \\ k &= -\dfrac{\ln0.5}{5730} \\ &= \dfrac{\ln2}{5730} \end{aligned}$$
No penalty for writing $k=0.0001$ to 4 d.p.

The leaf has $9\%$ of its original amount, so $Q=0.09Q_0$.
$$\begin{aligned} 0.09Q_0 &= Q_0e^{-kt} \\ 0.09 &= e^{-kt} \end{aligned}$$
Using $k=-\dfrac{\ln0.5}{5730}$, this is
$$0.09=e^{\frac{\ln0.5}{5730}t}$$
Taking logarithms:
$$\begin{aligned} \ln0.09 &= \dfrac{\ln0.5}{5730}\,t \\ t &= \dfrac{5730\ln0.09}{\ln0.5} \\ &\approx 19\,906 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{the leaf is about } 19\,906 \text{ years old}$$
No penalty for incorrect rounding.
criteria: Correct equation $0.09=e^{-kt}$ or similar, or equivalent merit

$$\begin{aligned} 4x^3-6x^2 &= 0 \\ 2x^2(2x-3) &= 0 \end{aligned}$$
so $x=0$ or $x=\dfrac{3}{2}$.

At $x=\dfrac{3}{2}$, $y''=9>0$, so the curve is concave up: a minimum turning point at $\left(\dfrac{3}{2},-\dfrac{11}{16}\right)$.

At $x=0$, $y''=0$, so the test is inconclusive and this is a possible horizontal point of inflexion.

Possible points of inflexion occur when $y''=0$:
$$12x(x-1)=0$$
so $x=0$ or $x=1$.

Test the concavity either side:
$$\begin{aligned} y''&=24>0 &&\text{at } x=-1 &&\text{concave up}\\ y''&=0 &&\text{at } x=0 &&\\ y''&=-3<0 &&\text{at } x=0.5 &&\text{concave down}\\ y''&=0 &&\text{at } x=1 &&\\ y''&=24>0 &&\text{at } x=2 &&\text{concave up} \end{aligned}$$
The concavity changes at both $x=0$ and $x=1$.

Since $y'=0$ at $x=0$, there is a horizontal point of inflexion at $(0,1)$. There is also a point of inflexion at $(1,0)$.

Let $A_n$ be the amount owing after $n$ months.

Show that after seven months, the total amount Sergio owes is:

$$A_7=12500\times1.0075-R(6\times1.0075+1)$$
Calculate the monthly repayment \$$R$ required to pay back the loan, correct to the nearest dollar.

solutions.latex:
In the first six months no interest is charged, so each repayment reduces the balance by $R$:
$$A_1=12\,500-R,\quad A_2=12\,500-2R,\quad A_3=12\,500-3R$$
so $A_6=12\,500-6R$.

The monthly rate is $r=\dfrac{0.09}{12}=0.0075$.

In month 7, interest is added and then $R$ is paid:
$$\begin{aligned} A_7 &= A_6\times1.0075-R \\ &= (12\,500-6R)\times1.0075-R \\ &= 12\,500\times1.0075-6R\times1.0075-R \\ &= 12\,500\times1.0075-R(6\times1.0075+1) \end{aligned}$$
as required.

solutions.latex:
Continue the pattern, interest then repayment each month:
$$A_8=A_7\times1.0075-R=12\,500\times1.0075^2-R(6\times1.0075^2+1.0075+1)$$
$$A_9=12\,500\times1.0075^3-R(6\times1.0075^3+1.0075^2+1.0075+1)$$
Hence
$$A_n=12\,500\times1.0075^{n-6}-R\left(6\times1.0075^{n-6}+1+1.0075+\cdots+1.0075^{n-7}\right)$$
The loan lasts $n=5\times12=60$ months:
$$A_{60}=12\,500\times1.0075^{54}-R\left(6\times1.0075^{54}+\left(1+1.0075+\cdots+1.0075^{53}\right)\right)$$
The bracketed sum is a G.P. with $a=1$, $r=1.0075$ and $54$ terms, so its sum is $\dfrac{1.0075^{54}-1}{1.0075-1}$.

The loan is repaid, so $A_{60}=0$:
$$12\,500\times1.0075^{54}=R\left(6\times1.0075^{54}+\dfrac{1.0075^{54}-1}{0.0075}\right)$$
$$\begin{aligned} R &= \dfrac{12\,500\times1.0075^{54}}{6\times1.0075^{54}+\frac{1.0075^{54}-1}{0.0075}} \\ &\approx \$248.66 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ R\approx\$249$$

parts.latex: Which of the following is equivalent to $\dfrac{1}{1-\sin\theta} + \dfrac{1}{1+\sin\theta}$?

parts.latex: Find $f'(x)$.

solutions.latex:
Using the quotient rule, $\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\dfrac{u}{v}\right)=\dfrac{u'v-uv'}{v^2}$, with
$$\begin{aligned} u&=x & v&=x^2-1\\ u'&=1 & v'&=2x\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} f'(x) &= \dfrac{x^2 - 1 - 2x^2}{\left(x^2-1\right)^2} \\ &= \dfrac{-x^2 - 1}{\left(x^2-1\right)^2} \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore f'(x) = \dfrac{-x^2 - 1}{\left(x^2-1\right)^2}$$
criteria: Uses the quotient rule, or equivalent merit

Find the point and the gradient at $x=2$.
$$f(2) = \dfrac{2}{2^2 - 1} = \dfrac{2}{3}$$

The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, so

The equation of the normal is

2547.stem:
The sum of the first $n$ terms in an arithmetic series is given by the formula

$$S_n = 3n^2 - 17n$$

where $n > 0$.

parts.latex: Show that the common difference is 6.
Hence, find the tenth term in the series.

solutions.latex:
The series is arithmetic, so $a = S_1$ and $T_2 = S_2 - S_1$.
$$S_1 = 3(1)^2 - 17(1) = -14$$
so $a=-14$.
$$S_2 = 3(2)^2 - 17(2) = -22$$
$$T_2 = -22 - (-14) = -8$$
The common difference is
$$\begin{aligned} d &= T_2 - T_1 \\ &= -8 - (-14) \\ &= 6 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Finds the first term of the arithmetic series, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
Using $T_n = a + (n-1)d$ with $a=-14$ and $d=6$,
$$\begin{aligned} T_{10} &= -14 + (10 - 1) \times 6 \\ &= 40 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Applies the correct formula, or equivalent merit

Solve $2\sin^2 x - 5\sin x\cos x + 3\cos^2 x = 0$, for $x \in [0, 2\pi]$.

solutions.latex:
Factorise the left side.
$$\begin{aligned} 2\sin^2 x - 5\sin x\cos x + 3\cos^2 x &= 0 \\ (2\sin x - 3\cos x)(\sin x - \cos x) &= 0 \end{aligned}$$
Case 1: $2\sin x = 3\cos x$, so $\tan x = \dfrac{3}{2}$.
$$x = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right) \text{ or } x = \pi + \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right)$$

parts.latex:
Let $f'(x) = x^2 + kx$.

The line $y = 2x + 1$ is a tangent to the graph of $y = f(x)$ at the point where $x = -1$.

Find $f(x)$.

solutions.latex:
Integrating $f'(x)$,
$$f(x) = \dfrac{1}{3}x^3 + \dfrac{1}{2}kx^2 + c$$
The tangent $y = 2x + 1$ touches the curve at $x = -1$, so $f'(-1) = 2$ and $f(-1) = 2(-1) + 1 = -1$.

From $f'(-1) = 2$:
$$(-1)^2 + k(-1) = 2$$
$$\therefore k = -1$$
From $f(-1) = -1$:
$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{1}{3}(-1)^3 + \dfrac{1}{2}k(-1)^2 + c &= -1 \\ \dfrac{1}{2}k + c &= -\dfrac{2}{3} \\ \dfrac{1}{2}\times(-1) + c &= -\dfrac{2}{3} \\ c &= -\dfrac{1}{6} \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore f(x) = \dfrac{1}{3}x^3 - \dfrac{1}{2}x^2 - \dfrac{1}{6}$$
criteria: Makes progress towards solution, or equivalent merit
Finds a valid primitive function, or equivalent merit

parts.latex: What are the values of $X$ and $Y$?

The account balance, $\$A_n$, at the end of $n$ months is given by the recurrence relation

$$A_n = \left(A_{n-1} + 500\right) \times q$$

What is the value of $q$?
Find the time, to the nearest whole month, that it takes for Sienna to reach her savings goal.

solutions.latex:
Interest for the first month is the monthly rate times the balance of $\$500$.
$$X = \dfrac{4.2\%}{12}\times 500 = \$1.75$$
The balance is the previous balance, plus the deposit, plus the interest.
$$Y = 1005.26 + 500 + 5.27 = \$1510.53$$
criteria: Finds the value of $X$ or $Y$, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
The monthly growth factor is
$$q = 1 + \dfrac{4.2\%}{12} = 1.0035$$

Build up the balance month by month.
$$A_1 = 500\times 1.0035$$
$$\begin{aligned} A_2 &= \left(500(1.0035) + 500\right)\times 1.0035 \\ &= 500(1.0035)^2 + 500(1.0035) \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} A_3 &= \left(500(1.0035)^2 + 500(1.0035) + 500\right)\times 1.0035 \\ &= 500(1.0035)^3 + 500(1.0035)^2 + 500(1.0035) \\ &= 500(1.0035)\left(1 + 1.0035 + 1.0035^2\right) \end{aligned}$$
Continuing the pattern, the bracket is a geometric series with $a = 1$, $r = 1.0035$ and $n$ terms.
$$A_n = 500(1.0035)\left(1 + 1.0035 + 1.0035^2 + \cdots + 1.0035^{n-1}\right)$$
Set $A_n = 50\,000$ and use the sum of a GP.
$$\begin{aligned} 50\,000 &= 500(1.0035)\times\dfrac{1.0035^n - 1}{0.0035} \\ \dfrac{2707}{2007} &= 1.0035^n \\ n &= \dfrac{\log\left(\frac{2707}{2007}\right)}{\log 1.0035} \\ &\approx 85.64 \end{aligned}$$
Therefore it will take 86 months for Sienna to reach her savings goal.
criteria: Makes progress towards solution, or equivalent merit
Expresses $A_n$ in terms of a geometric progression, or equivalent merit

2558.stem:
As a particle moves, its velocity, in metres per second, is described by the equation

$$v(t) = -2t^2 + 2t + 4$$

where $t \geq 0$ is the time in seconds. The particle is initially 4 metres right of the origin.

parts.latex: Find the time taken for the particle to reach its maximum velocity.
Find the position of the particle when it first comes to rest.
Find the total distance travelled by the particle in the first 3 seconds.

solutions.latex:
Method 1: maximum velocity occurs when $a(t) = 0$.

Differentiating $v(t) = -2t^2 + 2t + 4$,
$$a(t) = -4t + 2$$
$$\begin{aligned} -4t + 2 &= 0 \\ t &= 0.5 \text{ seconds} \end{aligned}$$
Method 2: since velocity is a quadratic function, the maximum is at the vertex.
$$t = -\dfrac{b}{2a} = -\dfrac{2}{2(-2)} = 0.5 \text{ seconds}$$
criteria: Attempts to solve $a(t) = 0$, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
The particle is at rest when $v(t) = 0$.
$$v(t) = 0 \text{ gives } t = -1 \text{ or } t = 2$$
Since $t \ge 0$, it first comes to rest at $t = 2$.

Since $x(0) = 4$, the position at $t = 2$ is
$$\begin{aligned} x(2) &= 4 + \displaystyle\int_0^2 v(t)\,dt \\ &= 4 + \left[-\dfrac{2}{3}t^3 + t^2 + 4t\right]_0^2 \\ &= 10\dfrac{2}{3} \end{aligned}$$
The particle is $10\dfrac{2}{3}$ metres to the right of the origin.
criteria: Finds the distance travelled in the first two seconds, or equivalent merit
Finds the time the particle comes to rest, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
The particle changes direction at $t = 2$, so the distance is the sum of the magnitudes of the displacements on $[0,2]$ and $[2,3]$.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Distance travelled} &= \int_0^2 v(t)\,dt + \left|\int_2^3 v(t)\,dt\right| \\ &= 6\dfrac{2}{3} - \int_2^3 v(t)\,dt \\ &= 6\dfrac{2}{3} - \left[-\dfrac{2}{3}t^3 + t^2 + 4t\right]_2^3 \\ &= 6\dfrac{2}{3} - \left[\left(-\dfrac{2}{3}(3)^3 + (3)^2 + 4(3)\right) - \left(-\dfrac{2}{3}(2)^3 + (2)^2 + 4(2)\right)\right] \\ &= 10\dfrac{1}{3} \text{ metres}\end{aligned}$$
criteria: Finds the distance travelled by the particle in the third second, or equivalent merit

figures.cap: cylinder of radius r on a cube

solutions.latex:
The volume is the cylinder plus the cube of side $2r$.
$$\pi r^2 h + (2r)^3 = 1.5$$
$$h = \dfrac{1.5 - 8r^3}{\pi r^2}$$
The coated surface is the 6 faces of the cube plus the curved surface of the cylinder. Let $S$ be this area.
$$S = 6\times(2r)^2 + 2\pi rh$$
Substituting $h$,
$$\begin{aligned} S(r) &= 24r^2 + 2\pi r\left(\dfrac{1.5 - 8r^3}{\pi r^2}\right) \\ &= 24r^2 + \dfrac{3 - 16r^3}{r} \end{aligned}$$
Differentiating,
$$S'(r) = 48r - \dfrac{3}{r^2} - 32r$$
For a stationary point, $S'(r) = 0$.
$$\begin{aligned} 16r &= \dfrac{3}{r^2} \\ r^3 &= \dfrac{3}{16} \end{aligned}$$
$$r = \sqrt[3]{\dfrac{3}{16}} \text{ since } r > 0$$
Test the nature using the sign of $S'(r)$.
$$\begin{aligned} S'(r) &< 0 &&\text{for } r \text{ just below } \sqrt[3]{\dfrac{3}{16}} &&\text{decreasing}\\ S'(r) &= 0 &&\text{at } r = \sqrt[3]{\dfrac{3}{16}} &&\text{stationary}\\ S'(r) &> 0 &&\text{for } r \text{ just above } \sqrt[3]{\dfrac{3}{16}} &&\text{increasing} \end{aligned}$$
So this is a minimum.
$$S_{\min} = 24\left(\sqrt[3]{\dfrac{3}{16}}\right)^2 + \dfrac{3 - 16\times\frac{3}{16}}{\sqrt[3]{\frac{3}{16}}} \approx 7.86 \text{ m}^2$$
The minimum surface area is $7.86 \text{ m}^2$ (to 2 d.p.).
criteria: Finds the value of $r$ that minimises the surface area, or equivalent merit
Finds the derivative of their equation for surface area, or equivalent merit
Finds an equation for the surface area in terms of one variable, or equivalent merit

parts.latex: Show that the $x$-coordinate of $A$ is $\ln 4$.
Hence, find the exact area enclosed by the curves and the $y$-axis. Express your answer in the form $\ln a + b$, where $a$ and $b$ are integers.

solutions.latex:
At the intersection the $y$ values are equal.
$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{3e^x}{e^x + 2} &= e^x - 2 \\ 3e^x &= (e^x - 2)(e^x + 2) \\ 3e^x &= e^{2x} - 4 \\ e^{2x} - 3e^x - 4 &= 0 \\ (e^x + 1)(e^x - 4) &= 0 \end{aligned}$$
Since $e^x > 0$, $e^x \ne -1$, so $e^x = 4$.
$$\therefore x = \ln 4$$

$$\begin{aligned}\text{Area} &= \int_0^{\ln 4} \left(\dfrac{3e^x}{e^x + 2} - \left(e^x - 2\right)\right)dx \\ &= \int_0^{\ln 4} \left(\dfrac{3e^x}{e^x + 2} - e^x + 2\right)dx \\ &= \left[3\ln\left(e^x + 2\right) - e^x + 2x\right]_0^{\ln 4} \\ &= \left(3\ln 6 - 4 + 2\ln 4\right) - \left(3\ln 3 - 1 + 0\right) \\ &= \ln 128 - 3 \text{ units}^2\end{aligned}$$

2561.stem:
The continuous random variable $X$ has a median value of $m$ and a probability density function given by:

$$f(x) = \begin{cases} kx & \text{if } 0 \leq x < 1 \\ kx^2 & \text{if } 1 \leq x \leq 3 \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}$$

parts.latex: Show that $k = \dfrac{6}{55}$.
Find the cumulative distribution function of $X$.
Find the value of $m$, correct to two decimal places.

solutions.latex:
The total probability is 1.
$$\displaystyle\int_0^1 kx\,dx + \int_1^3 kx^2\,dx = 1$$
$$\begin{aligned} \left[\dfrac{k}{2}x^2\right]_0^1 + \left[\dfrac{k}{3}x^3\right]_1^3 &= 1 \\ \dfrac{k}{2} + \left(9k - \dfrac{k}{3}\right) &= 1 \\ \dfrac{55}{6}k &= 1 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore k = \dfrac{6}{55}$$
criteria: Writes a valid equation involving the sum of all probabilities, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
For $0 \le x < 1$:
$$\begin{aligned} F(x) &= \dfrac{6}{55}\displaystyle\int_0^x t\,dt \\ &= \dfrac{6}{55}\left[\dfrac{1}{2}t^2\right]_0^x \\ &= \dfrac{3}{55}x^2 \end{aligned}$$
For $1 \le x \le 3$:
$$\begin{aligned} F(x) &= \dfrac{3}{55} + \dfrac{6}{55}\displaystyle\int_1^x t^2\,dt \\ &= \dfrac{3}{55} + \dfrac{6}{55}\left[\dfrac{1}{3}t^3\right]_1^x \\ &= \dfrac{3}{55} + \dfrac{2}{55}x^3 - \dfrac{2}{55} \\ &= \dfrac{1}{55} + \dfrac{2}{55}x^3 \end{aligned}$$
Therefore
$$F(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{3}{55}x^2 & \text{if } 0 \le x < 1 \\[6pt] \dfrac{1}{55} + \dfrac{2}{55}x^3 & \text{if } 1 \le x \le 3 \end{cases}$$
criteria: Makes progress towards solution, or equivalent merit
Describes the cumulative distribution function using an integral, or equivalent merit

meta.format_note: Changed dummy variable in integrals from x to t (same mathematics).

solutions.latex:
Since $F(1) = \dfrac{3}{55} < 0.5$, the median satisfies $1 \le m < 3$, so use the second piece with $F(m) = 0.5$.
$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{1}{55} + \dfrac{2}{55}m^3 &= 0.5 \\ 2 + 4m^3 &= 55 \\ m &= \sqrt[3]{\dfrac{53}{4}} \\ &\approx 2.37 \end{aligned}$$
The median is $m \approx 2.37$ (to 2 d.p.).
criteria: Recognises that $1 \le m < 3$, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
Two surveyors, $A$ and $B$, stand on level ground to observe a large tree. The tree is directly north of surveyor $A$ who sights the top of the tree at an angle of elevation of $52^\circ$.

Surveyor $B$ is 27 metres away from Surveyor $A$ on a bearing of $043^\circ$ and sights the top of the tree at an angle of elevation of $46^\circ$.

Find the height, $h$, of the tree correct to the nearest metre.
parts.note: 3D trigonometry (tree seen from two points on level ground, elevation and bearings) is now Year 11 Extension 1, not Advanced.

solutions.latex:
\exfigure{833_q29_s1}

Let $C$ be the point at the base of the tree. Using the tangent ratio in the two right-angled triangles,
$$AC = \dfrac{h}{\tan 52^\circ}, \qquad BC = \dfrac{h}{\tan 46^\circ}$$
In $\triangle ABC$, $AB = 27$ and $\angle CAB = 43^\circ$ (the bearing of $B$ from $A$ is $043^\circ$ and $C$ is due north of $A$). Apply the cosine rule.
$$\left(\dfrac{h}{\tan 46^\circ}\right)^2 = \left(\dfrac{h}{\tan 52^\circ}\right)^2 + 27^2 - 2\times\dfrac{h}{\tan 52^\circ}\times 27\times\cos 43^\circ$$
Rearranging,
$$\begin{aligned} 0 &= \left(\dfrac{1}{\tan^2 52^\circ} - \dfrac{1}{\tan^2 46^\circ}\right)h^2 - \dfrac{54\cos 43^\circ}{\tan 52^\circ}h + 27^2 \\ 0 &\approx -0.32215h^2 - 30.85539h + 729 \end{aligned}$$
Using the quadratic formula, with $h > 0$,
$$h = \dfrac{30.855\ldots - \sqrt{30.855\ldots^2 - 4\times(-0.322\ldots)\times 729}}{2\times(-0.322\ldots)} \approx 19.6$$
$$\therefore h \approx 20 \text{ metres (to the nearest metre)}$$
criteria: Makes progress in solving for $h$, or equivalent merit
Forms a relationship, in terms of $h$, between the edges in the base triangle, or equivalent merit
Expresses the edge $AC$ in terms of $h$, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
A population, $P$, which is initially 40 500, varies according to the formula $P = 40500\,b^{\frac{-t}{5}}$ where $b$ is a positive constant and $t$ is time in years, $t \ge 0$

The population is 1500 after 15 years.

Find the value of $t$, correct to one decimal place, for which the instantaneous rate of decrease is 25 people per year.

solutions.latex:
Substitute $P = 1500$, $t = 15$ to find $b$.
$$\begin{aligned} 1500 &= 40500\,b^{-\frac{15}{5}} \\ \dfrac{1}{27} &= b^{-3} \\ 27 &= b^3 \\ b &= 3 \end{aligned}$$
We want $t$ when $\dfrac{dP}{dt} = -25$.

Using $y = a^x$, $y' = \ln a \cdot a^x$ on $P = 40500 \times 3^{-\frac{t}{5}}$:
$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{dP}{dt} &= 40500 \times \dfrac{-1}{5}\ln 3 \times 3^{-\frac{t}{5}} \\ &= -8100\ln 3 \times 3^{-\frac{t}{5}} \end{aligned}$$
Set this equal to $-25$.
$$\begin{aligned} -8100\ln 3 \times 3^{-\frac{t}{5}} &= -25 \\ 3^{-\frac{t}{5}} &= \dfrac{1}{324\ln 3} \\ -\dfrac{t}{5} &= \dfrac{\ln\left(\frac{1}{324\ln 3}\right)}{\ln 3} \\ t &= \dfrac{-5\ln\left(\frac{1}{324\ln 3}\right)}{\ln 3} \\ &= 26.737\ldots \\ &\approx 26.7 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ t \approx 26.7 \text{ years}$$
criteria: Finds $b$, sets $\dfrac{dP}{dt}=-25$ and finds a correct derivative, or equivalent merit

The volume of a cylinder is $V = \pi r^2 h$, and $V = 380$, so we make $h$ the subject.

Substitute into $A = 2\pi r^2 + 2\pi rh$.
$$\begin{aligned} A &= 2\pi r^2 + 2\pi r\left(\dfrac{380}{\pi r^2}\right) \\ &= 2\pi r^2 + \dfrac{760\pi r}{\pi r^2} \\ &= 2\pi r^2 + \dfrac{760}{r} \end{aligned}$$

Since $r > 0$, $\dfrac{d^2A}{dr^2} > 0$, therefore $A$ has a minimum value.

2600.stem: Find the first derivative of the following functions:

parts.latex: $y = \ln\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{x}}{x^2+1}\right)$
$f(x) = \tan^3 2x$
$y = e^{\cos 2x}\cos 2x$

solutions.latex:
Using the log laws $\ln\dfrac{a}{b}=\ln a-\ln b$ and $\ln a^n=n\ln a$:
$$y=\dfrac{1}{2}\ln x-\ln(x^2+1)$$
Differentiating,
$$\therefore\ \dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{1}{2x}-\dfrac{2x}{x^2+1}$$
criteria: Applies the log laws correctly, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
Using the chain rule, with $u=\tan 2x$ and $\dfrac{d}{dx}(\tan 2x)=2\sec^2 2x$:
$$\begin{aligned} f'(x) &= 3\tan^2 2x\cdot\sec^2 2x\cdot 2 \\ &= 6\tan^2 2x\sec^2 2x \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ f'(x)=6\tan^2 2x\sec^2 2x$$
criteria: Sets up the chain rule correctly, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
Using $\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(a^{kx}\right)=k\ln a\cdot a^{kx}$, and since $8^e$ is a constant:
$$\therefore\ \dfrac{dy}{dx}=e\ln 8\cdot 8^{ex}$$

Using the product rule, $\dfrac{d}{dx}(uv)=u'v+uv'$, with
$$\begin{aligned} u&=e^{\cos 2x} & v&=\cos 2x\\ u'&=-2\sin 2x\, e^{\cos 2x} & v'&=-2\sin 2x\end{aligned}$$
So
$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{dy}{dx} &= -2\sin 2x\, e^{\cos 2x}\cos 2x+e^{\cos 2x}(-2\sin 2x) \\ &= -2e^{\cos 2x}\sin 2x\,(1+\cos 2x) \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \dfrac{dy}{dx}=-2e^{\cos 2x}\sin 2x\,(1+\cos 2x)$$
criteria: Applies the product rule correctly in part, or equivalent merit

Expanding the square and using $\tan^2\theta=\sec^2\theta-1$:
$$\begin{aligned} \int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\left(1-\tan\dfrac{x}{2}\right)^2dx &= \int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\left(1-2\tan\dfrac{x}{2}+\tan^2\dfrac{x}{2}\right)dx \\ &= \int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\left(\sec^2\dfrac{x}{2}-2\tan\dfrac{x}{2}\right)dx \\ &= \left[2\tan\dfrac{x}{2}+4\ln\left|\cos\dfrac{x}{2}\right|\right]_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \\ &= 2+4\ln\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right) \\ &= 2+\ln\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right) \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\left(1-\tan\dfrac{x}{2}\right)^2dx=2+\ln\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)$$

Dividing by 2,

parts.latex: Find the stationary point and determine its nature.
Find any point of inflection.
Sketch the function showing all important features.
Find an estimation to the area under the graph in the domain $[0, 2]$ using the Trapezoidal rule with three function values.
Explain whether the Trapezoidal rule over estimated or under estimated the exact area in part (d).

solutions.latex:
Using the product rule, $\dfrac{d}{dx}(uv)=u'v+uv'$, with
$$\begin{aligned} u&=4x & v&=e^{-x}\\ u'&=4 & v'&=-e^{-x}\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{dy}{dx} &= 4e^{-x}-4xe^{-x} \\ &= 4e^{-x}(1-x) \end{aligned}$$
Stationary points occur where $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=0$. Since $e^{-x}>0$, $x=1$, and $y=4e^{-1}$.

To find the nature, use the second derivative:
$$\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}=-4e^{-x}(2-x)$$
At $x=1$,
$$\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}=-4e^{-1}<0$$
$$\therefore\ (1,4e^{-1})\text{ is a maximum turning point}$$
criteria: Finds the stationary point and tests its nature, or equivalent merit
Finds the stationary point, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
A point of inflection needs $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}=0$:
$$-4e^{-x}(2-x)=0$$
Since $e^{-x}>0$, $x=2$. Test the concavity either side:
$$\begin{aligned} x=1.9:\ & \dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}<0 &&\text{concave down}\\ x=2.1:\ & \dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}>0 &&\text{concave up}\end{aligned}$$
The concavity changes, and $y=8e^{-2}$ when $x=2$.
$$\therefore\ (2,8e^{-2})\text{ is a point of inflection}$$

The curve passes through the origin, has a maximum at $(1,4e^{-1})$ and an inflection at $(2,8e^{-2})$, and approaches the $x$-axis as $x\to\infty$.

By the trapezoidal rule,
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Area} &\approx \dfrac{1}{2}\left(0+4e^{-1}\right)+\dfrac{1}{2}\left(4e^{-1}+8e^{-2}\right) \\ &= 4\left(e^{-1}+e^{-2}\right) \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{Area}\approx 4\left(e^{-1}+e^{-2}\right)\text{ units}^2$$

2606.stem: The water level, measured in meters, at a dam has been changing at a rate of $R = t^3 - 11t^2 + 35t - 29$ for $0 \le t \le 6$ years.

parts.latex: When is the water level decreasing most rapidly?
What is the change in water level of the dam for the 6 years?

solutions.latex:
The water level decreases most rapidly where $R$ is least, so find the stationary points of $R$:
$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{dR}{dt} &= 3t^2-22t+35 \\ &= (3t-7)(t-5) \end{aligned}$$
Setting $\dfrac{dR}{dt}=0$ gives $t=\dfrac{7}{3}$ or $t=5$.

Nature, using the second derivative $\dfrac{d^2R}{dt^2}=6t-22$:
$$\begin{aligned} t=\dfrac{7}{3}:\ & \dfrac{d^2R}{dt^2}=-8<0 &&\text{maximum}\\ t=5:\ & \dfrac{d^2R}{dt^2}=8>0 &&\text{minimum, } R=-4\end{aligned}$$
Check the endpoints of the domain:
$$\begin{aligned} t=0:\ & R=-29\\ t=6:\ & R=1\end{aligned}$$
The least value of $R$ is $-29$.
$$\therefore\ \text{the water level decreases most rapidly at } t=0$$
criteria: Finds the stationary points and their nature, or equivalent merit
Finds the stationary points, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
The change in level is the integral of the rate:
$$\begin{aligned} \int_0^6\left(t^3-11t^2+35t-29\right)dt &= \left[\dfrac{t^4}{4}-\dfrac{11t^3}{3}+\dfrac{35t^2}{2}-29t\right]_0^6 \\ &= -12 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{the water level decreased by } 12 \text{ m}$$
criteria: Writes the correct integral, or equivalent merit
